name: Transfer Pricing
title: Transfer Pricing
answer: Transfer pricing covers the prices and terms that related companies in different tax jurisdictions set for transactions between them, including goods, services, loans, royalties, and cost sharing arrangements. The core test is the arm's length principle, which asks whether the terms would be what unrelated parties would agree to in comparable circumstances. In practice the scope reaches functional analysis, comparability studies, local files, master files, country by country reports, and dispute resolution through mutual agreement procedures or advance pricing arrangements. For AI related businesses the scope also includes cloud compute, data access, model licensing, and the allocation of costs for developing and maintaining AI systems.

sections.body: Transfer pricing covers the prices and terms that related companies in different tax jurisdictions set for transactions between them, including goods, services, loans, royalties, and cost sharing arrangements. The core test is the arm's length principle, which asks whether the terms would be what unrelated parties would agree to in comparable circumstances. In practice the scope reaches functional analysis, comparability studies, local files, master files, country by country reports, and dispute resolution through mutual agreement procedures or advance pricing arrangements. For AI related businesses the scope also includes cloud compute, data access, model licensing, and the allocation of costs for developing and maintaining AI systems.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on financial and operational data pulled from enterprise resource planning systems, general ledgers, intercompany accounting modules, and contract repositories. Teams also rely on benchmarking databases, tax research services, spreadsheets, and document management platforms to store and version their analyses. Where AI is used, it typically runs on data pipelines that extract and normalize transaction records, on cloud compute for model training or use, and on application programming interfaces that connect tax systems to analytics tools. Data quality, consistent entity identifiers, and clear audit trails matter more than the specific model choice.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method starts with a functional analysis that identifies what each related party does, what assets it uses, and what risks it assumes. From there the team selects a transfer pricing method, such as the comparable uncontrolled price method, the resale price method, the cost plus method, the transactional net margin method, or the profit split method, and then searches for comparable transactions or companies. AI can assist by using natural language processing to read contracts and invoices, clustering to group potential comparables, and anomaly detection to flag unusual intercompany charges. The output is a documented set of prices, margins, or profit allocations that supports the tax return and the local file.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in transfer pricing turn on documentation, consistency, and the ability to defend the chosen prices under audit. Tax authorities may challenge the results, impose penalties for inadequate documentation, and propose adjustments that lead to double taxation, which taxpayers can seek to resolve through mutual agreement procedures or advance pricing arrangements. Provenance matters because every figure in a local file should trace back to a source system, a contract, or a benchmarking study, with version control and a clear record of who changed what and when. When AI is used, governance also covers model validation, explainability, data privacy, cross border data transfer rules, and the risk of fabricated or unsupported outputs.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Transfer pricing is moving toward more continuous monitoring, with tax authorities and companies both using data analytics to spot anomalies earlier and to test prices in near real time. AI related intangibles, data, and cloud services are likely to attract more scrutiny as tax rules try to keep pace with how value is created. Documentation may become more automated, with models drafting first versions of local files and benchmarking memos from structured data. Dispute prevention, through better contemporaneous evidence and cooperative compliance programs, is likely to grow alongside traditional audit defense.
